# eslint-plugin-mcp-sdk-security

Guide for AI coding assistants using this plugin in a project. To change the plugin's own source, read https://github.com/ofri-peretz/eslint/blob/main/AGENTS.md instead.

> ESLint MCP security rules for the Model Context Protocol SDK — follows tool arguments into shells, file paths, URLs, SQL and eval; catches credential leaks, untrusted text in model-facing descriptions and prompts, unhardened HTTP transports, shared stateless servers, predictable session ids, untrusted stdio commands and schema/handler drift.

## Enable it

```bash
npm install --save-dev eslint-plugin-mcp-sdk-security
```

Requires ESLint ^8.40.0 || ^9.0.0 || ^10.0.0 and Node >=22.13.0.

Flat config files (`eslint.config.*`) are found by ESLint 8.57 and newer; on ESLint 9 and 10 they are the default.

```js
// eslint.config.mjs
import mcpSdkSecurity from 'eslint-plugin-mcp-sdk-security';

export default [mcpSdkSecurity.configs.recommended];
```

Each preset is one flat config object: put it in the array as an element, do not spread it. Rule ids are prefixed `mcp-sdk-security/`. Add it to the config you already have; do not remove other plugins. TypeScript files need a TypeScript parser in the config (`typescript-eslint`).

Use it alongside `eslint-plugin-security`, not instead of it: keep that plugin if the project has it. Measured overlap and the limits of both: https://eslint.interlace.tools/docs/getting-started/with-eslint-plugin-security

## Presets

| Preset        | Rules | Errors | Warnings |
| ------------- | ----- | ------ | -------- |
| `minimal`     | 2     | 2      | 0        |
| `recommended` | 15    | 14     | 1        |
| `strict`      | 15    | 14     | 1        |

### `minimal`

2 rules:

- `no-command-injection-in-tool` (error): Disallow an MCP tool argument choosing the command a child_process call runs.
- `require-tool-input-schema` (error): Require an input schema when an MCP tool handler reads arguments.

### `recommended`

15 rules:

- `no-code-injection-in-tool` (error): Disallow an MCP tool argument reaching eval, new Function or a vm context as code.
- `no-command-injection-in-tool` (error): Disallow an MCP tool argument choosing the command a child_process call runs.
- `no-credential-leak-in-tool` (error): Disallow an MCP tool returning the server's environment or the caller's token, or forwarding that token upstream.
- `no-duplicate-tool-name` (warn): Disallow registering or listing two MCP tools with the same name on one server.
- `no-path-traversal-in-tool` (error): Disallow an MCP tool argument choosing the file an fs call reads, writes or deletes without a containment check.
- `no-predictable-session-id` (error): Disallow an MCP sessionIdGenerator that returns a counter, a timestamp, Math.random() or a constant.
- `no-shared-stateless-transport` (error): Disallow sharing one stateless Streamable HTTP transport or one MCP server across requests.
- `no-sql-injection-in-tool` (error): Disallow an MCP tool argument reaching the text of a SQL query instead of its parameters.
- `no-ssrf-in-tool` (error): Disallow an MCP tool argument choosing the host an outbound HTTP request is sent to.
- `no-tool-description-injection` (error): Disallow MCP tool, prompt and resource descriptions built from text a client, a remote service or a file controls.
- `no-untrusted-stdio-command` (error): Disallow an MCP client spawning a stdio server whose command comes from a tool argument, a network response or a project config file.
- `no-untrusted-tool-metadata-in-prompt` (error): Disallow an MCP client writing a server's tool, prompt or resource metadata into an LLM prompt instead of its tool definitions.
- `no-unvalidated-tool-args` (error): Disallow a tool handler reading an argument its declared input schema does not include.
- `require-http-transport-hardening` (error): Require an MCP HTTP server transport to validate the Host header and a network-reachable MCP server to authenticate its callers.
- `require-tool-input-schema` (error): Require an input schema when an MCP tool handler reads arguments.

### `strict`

Same rules as `recommended`.

## Other Interlace plugins by dependency

If the project also depends on one of these, add the matching plugin the same way:

- `express`, `fastify`, `koa`, `@hapi/hapi`, `restify`, `hono`, `next`, `@nestjs/core`, `@nestjs/common`, `aws-lambda`, `@types/aws-lambda`, `@middy/core`, `commander`, `yargs`, `@oclif/core`, `@modelcontextprotocol/*`: `eslint-plugin-node-security`
- `express`: `eslint-plugin-express-security`
- `@nestjs/common`, `@nestjs/core`: `eslint-plugin-nestjs-security`
- `react`, `react-dom`, `preact`, `vue`, `svelte`, `@angular/core`, `solid-js`, `lit`, `next`, `nuxt`: `eslint-plugin-browser-security`
- `jsonwebtoken`, `jose`, `express-jwt`, `@nestjs/jwt`, `jwks-rsa`, `jwt-decode`: `eslint-plugin-jwt-security`
- `pg`, `pg-pool`, `pg-promise`, `postgres`, `slonik`: `eslint-plugin-postgresql-security`
- `mysql2`, `mysql`: `eslint-plugin-mysql-security`
- `mongodb`, `mongoose`: `eslint-plugin-mongodb-security`
- `better-sqlite3`, `sqlite3`: `eslint-plugin-sqlite-security`
- `knex`: `eslint-plugin-knex-security`
- `@prisma/client`, `prisma`: `eslint-plugin-prisma-security`
- `drizzle-orm`: `eslint-plugin-drizzle-security`
- `sequelize`: `eslint-plugin-sequelize-security`
- `typeorm`: `eslint-plugin-typeorm-security`
- `@supabase/supabase-js`: `eslint-plugin-supabase-security`
- `@grpc/reflection`, `grpc-server-reflection`: `eslint-plugin-grpc-security`
- `openai`, `@openai/agents`: `eslint-plugin-openai-security`
- `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`: `eslint-plugin-anthropic-security`
- `@google/genai`: `eslint-plugin-gemini-security`
- `ai`: `eslint-plugin-vercel-ai-security`
- `aws-lambda`, `@types/aws-lambda`, `@middy/core`: `eslint-plugin-lambda-security`

The full stack-to-plugin playbook (with config rendering and a proof step) is the `security-linting` skill: https://github.com/ofri-peretz/eslint/tree/main/skills/security-linting
